idiom_name: shared service header + parallel function-pointer table
implementation_notes: C has no interfaces, so equivalence is a discipline rather than a compiler check: the service contract is a header declaring a struct of function pointers plus the agreed error and buffer-ownership conventions, and the proxy fills a table whose entries call the real implementation and then apply policy. Generate both tables from one definition so a missing or reordered slot cannot go unnoticed, and keep the policy state in the proxy struct rather than in globals. When the contract is a byte-stream or message API instead of an in-process interface, the same table sits in front of the transport calls rather than the business functions.
pitfalls: Nothing in the language checks that the proxy table implements the whole service table; a missing or mis-ordered slot is a null-pointer call at runtime, so both tables must be generated from one definition.
Return codes, errno and buffer ownership are part of a C interface: a proxy that maps errors into its own codes or frees the caller's buffer breaks equivalence.
Policy state shared by several threads (counters, token buckets) needs explicit synchronisation; a plain static counter silently corrupts under concurrency.

variants.name: Dynamic-linker interposition (LD_PRELOAD)
variants.implementation_notes: Where the service is a remote endpoint reached through libc, the proxy can front it without touching any caller: preload a shared object that resolves the real symbol with dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, ...), applies policy (timeouts, metrics, redirection to a local proxy) and then calls the real function. Equivalence holds at the libc boundary rather than at source level, so callers and the service binary stay exactly as they are - the price is that the interception is invisible, environment-driven and therefore fragile.
pitfalls: dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, ...) must be resolved once and cached; resolving per call is slow, and re-entering the wrapper can loop or deadlock.
The wrapper is active in every process that inherits the variable, including the proxy's own children: scope or unset LD_PRELOAD or the proxy intercepts itself.
Static binaries and direct syscalls bypass interposition entirely, so 'equivalent interface' silently holds for some callers and not others.
